clarifications: Can height be negative? No, all heights are non-negative.
What to return for an empty array? Return 0 as no water can be trapped.
Are heights guaranteed to fit in memory? Yes, they are within constraints.
Can there be duplicate heights? Yes, duplicates are allowed.
Should I account for water at the edges? No, water cannot be trapped at the edges.
Is the input array mutable? Assume it is not modified.
What if all bars are the same height? No water will be trapped.
expectedApproaches: Brute force with nested loops, O(n^2) time.
Dynamic programming with precomputed max heights, O(n) time and space.
Two-pointer technique, O(n) time and O(1) space.
solutions: Use two pointers starting from both ends of the array. Maintain left_max and right_max to store the maximum heights seen so far from the left and right, respectively. Move the pointers towards each other, updating the trapped water based on the minimum of left_max and right_max minus the current height.
commonMistakes: Using nested loops, leading to O(n^2) time complexity.
Failing to handle cases where no water is trapped.

hintLadder.text: What are the two highest bars that determine the water level over a segment?
Consider using two pointers to track the maximum heights from both ends.
Calculate trapped water by comparing current height with the minimum of left and right maximum heights.

Weak: Relies on a brute force approach with nested loops or fails to handle edge cases.
